The error 1152 occurs when an IBM SPSS compressed image is launched and files compressed within it are extracted to the temporary location. The possibility of these files being downloaded improperly exists. To resolve the issue, you can try the following:

1. Verify the file content using a tool such as MD5 to ensure the file was downloaded correctly.
2. Attempt downloading the trial version again and test.
3. Check the available space within the temporary location noted by the installer.
4. Ensure the ability to write in the temporary location noted by the installer.

Additionally, you can try harvesting the.msi and accompanying files required for silent install by following these steps:

1. Go to: Start > Run and type '%temp%' to navigate to the temporary path for Windows Installer programs. Delete all contents within this folder.
2. Run the installer executable (SPSS_Modeler_18.1_win64.exe) as normal. When it finishes extracting and decompressing the.msi file and the end-user is required to click 'Continue', minimise this window.
3. Switch to the %temp% folder and locate the folder with the 'ModelerClient64.msi' file. Copy ALL contents within this folder and paste it to a local folder (e.g. C:\Temp\Modeler\ClientInstall).
4. Once copied, switch back to the installation wizard and hit 'Cancel'.

Then, use the command prompt to execute the 'MsiExec' command:
MsiExec.exe /i "<path>\ModelerClient.msi" /qn /L*v logfile.txt INSTALLDIR="C:\Program Files\IBM\SPSS\Modeler\18.1" LICENSETYPE="Network" LSHOST="mylicserver"

Note: Replace "<path>" with the location of your.msi file. 

It is also recommended to delete the contents of the temporary folder as the Fix Pack and Client installations use the same file names to prevent accidental copying of the Client installation instead of the Fix Pack install. 

If the issue persists, refer to the 'NetworkLicenseAdministratorsGuide.pdf' for a full list of Silent Install options.

To resolve the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server, you can configure the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool as follows:

* Set the Minimum connections to 0 to avoid situations where a connection is kept in the pool to meet the minimum requirement, even though it may have been idle for longer than Unused timeout.
* Set the values for Unused timeout and Reap timeout so that the sum does not exceed any network level idle connection timeout.

Additionally, you can also try reducing the Minimum Connections to 0 on the data source, which will cause WAS to remove all connections after a period of inactivity. To do this, go to the WAS admin console, navigate to Resources -> JDBC -> Data sources, and for each of the db domains, select the Connection pools link and edit the settings.

It is also recommended to review the document "Troubleshooting stale connection problems" for further information on resolving the StaleConnectionException.

To determine when to use conversation sharing in DataPower MQ queue managers, consider the following information from the passages:

1. **IBM WebSphere MQ server version**: Conversation sharing is available in IBM WebSphere MQ server version 7.0 and later releases.
2. **Default settings**: The default setting of sharing conversations (SHARECNV) value is 0 in DataPower mq-qm object, while the default value for MQ SVRCONN channel is 10.
3. **Negotiated value**: The sharing conversations value is negotiated between MQ server and DataPower, and the lower value takes effect.
4. **Special consideration for DataPower firmware**: For DataPower firmware releases 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x, and earlier, use a negotiated sharing conversations value of 0 (Case #1). For firmware releases 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x, and later, you can use Case #2 or Case #3.
5. **Case #1**: Set a value of 0 or 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object to disable sharing conversations, regardless of the IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
6. **Case #2**: Set a value of 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute and select "on" in Share Single Conversation attribute of the mq-qm object to support IBM WebSphere MQ V7 and later release features with a single conversation per TCP/IP channel instance.
7. **Case #3**: Set a value of 2 or more on the Sharing Conversations attribute to support IBM WebSphere MQ 7 and later release features with 2 or more conversations per TCP/IP channel instance.
8. **Performance implications**: Using SHARECNV(10) can result in 15% slower processing of messages from client applications compared to SHARECNV(0).
9. **APAR requirement**: To use sharing conversations, ensure you have applied APAR IV24821 to the IBM WebSphere MQ server.
10. **Verifying configuration**: Verify the configuration empirically to ensure the IBM WebSphere MQ server can sustain the load from DataPower with the negotiated Sharing Conversations value.

To identify the negotiated Sharing Conversations status, use the following MQ commands:

* On distributed platforms: `runmqsc <qmgr> display chs(CHANNEL3) maxshcnv curshcnv`
* On z/OS systems: `connect to <qmgr>` and then issue the relevant commands.

When configuring conversation sharing on DataPower, consider the special values:
* 0: Disables sharing conversations
* 1: Enables sharing conversations with a single conversation per TCP/IP channel instance (Case #2)
* 2 or more: Enables sharing conversations with 2 or more conversations per TCP/IP channel instance (Case #3)
* 10 or less: Recommended value for the Sharing Conversations attribute to ensure the IBM WebSphere MQ server can sustain the load from DataPower.
